text:
emily: quick follow-up from the hosting-abstraction RFC — thinking we should separate two axes: 'capability manifests' (what the app needs) and 'binding profiles' (how hosting satisfies it).

raj: ok, can you give a concrete example? worried about breaking runtime handshake.

emily: short example:
```yaml
capabilities:
  streaming: true
  parallel_kv_cache: false
  kms: hsm
  max_latency_ms: 150
binding_profile: hosted
```

lina: so binding_profile would translate to runtime flags + secrets routing? e.g., hosted -> use cp-managed kms; private -> forward to customer-kms endpoint + local agent.

jon: big concern: private can't receive plaintext tokens from the control plane. we need a zero-knowledge handshake or KMS-proxy. avoid control-plane secret transfers.

emily: agreed. proposal: binding_profile includes 'secret_policy: forward-only | control-managed' and 'local_audit: true|false'.

ops-bot: NOTE: to comply with audits, 'local_audit: true' must enable local retention and write to the customer-specified sink (s3/gcs/onprem).

raj: how does fallback work? if dedicated is saturated, we route to hosted with degraded guarantees. need explicit downgrade semantics in the manifest.

lina: suggestion: add 'degrade_policy' to manifest with machine-readable tags so runtime can decide fallbacks (e.g., degrade_to: {model: small, latency_target_ms: 300}).

jon: also add a 'capability_version' field so we can do compatibility checks during handshake and fail fast on mismatch.

emily: ok. action items: 1) I'll open an RFC PR w/ sample manifest, gate matrix, and normative vs hint fields. 2) @raj to draft runtime handshake pseudo-protocol. 3) @lina add e2e test for private KMS flow. 4) @jon to outline audit-sink perms. Target sync next Tue.

lina: :thumbsup: I'll mock the YAML <-> runtime flags mapping this afternoon.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary test harness kicked off for binding-profile-v1, results will post to #eng-runtime.

raj: heads-up: document should make it explicit which fields are normative (runtime MUST honor) vs hints (runtime MAY ignore).
